title: Trilateral.org source-integrity and stale-metadata audit, 2026-08-08
summary: Audit of official-domain source contamination, placeholder content, and contradictory date/biography metadata that require field-level corroboration.

sources.title: UNE DESTINATION BORD DE MER TENDANCE - Deauville France

evidence.observation: The official publications index currently includes injected online-casino SEO text in Polish, French, and English ahead of the legitimate publication list.
The official trilateral.org domain serves a publication URL named deauville-casno-france containing unrelated French tourism/casino content and an outbound online-casino link.
Official region/contact and historical publication templates expose Lorem ipsum placeholder blocks and a fabricated placeholder attribution 'Frances Loremis'.

The T30/T31 page surfaces a related event titled '2018 European Regional Meeting' with a displayed date of August 31, 2021, demonstrating internally contradictory event metadata on the official domain.

gaps: The underlying cause of the casino content has not been established; it may reflect compromise, legacy CMS contamination, or other publishing failure.
The full domain has not been exhaustively scanned for injected pages or placeholder templates.
Archived snapshots and downloadable publication files should be compared against current HTML before historical content is normalized.
caveats: An official domain is still useful evidence, but domain ownership alone does not make every field or page trustworthy.
Do not call the site definitively hacked without infrastructure or incident evidence; describe the observed injected/spam-like content and integrity indicators.
Current roster inclusion can remain useful while biographies, event dates, and publication descriptions require independent freshness checks.

workflow.next_action: Add source-quality guards: reject known spam/placeholder text, corroborate mutable fields, and prefer downloadable/archived publication artifacts for historical extraction.

notes: The official domain currently contains clear unrelated casino SEO content and template placeholders; future scrapers need source-quality filtering.
The existence of contaminated HTML does not invalidate every official-domain record, but it destroys the assumption that official-domain text is uniformly authoritative.
Roster status, biography role text, publication descriptions, and event dates should have independent freshness/provenance checks.

classification_rules: Treat domain ownership and field correctness as separate confidence dimensions.
Reject obvious casino/SEO spam and Lorem ipsum placeholder text from normalized research content.
Flag internally contradictory dates instead of silently selecting one.
Corroborate mutable biographies and event metadata with independent authoritative sources.
Prefer original downloadable documents, archival snapshots, or primary institutional records for historical publications when current HTML is contaminated.
data.method: Inspected the current official publications index, an unrelated casino-content page on the official domain, regional contact templates, and historical publication pages for contamination and metadata contradictions.
data.narrative_role: source-integrity skeptic pass and scraper-quality guard generation
data.research_question: Can trilateral.org be treated as uniformly authoritative at the field level, or does the current site require contamination and freshness controls before normalization?

findings.finding: The official publications surface contains unrelated online-casino SEO content.
The official domain serves a standalone unrelated French casino/tourism publication page with an external casino link.
Multiple official templates contain Lorem ipsum placeholder content.
Official event metadata can be internally contradictory, including a '2018' event displayed with a 2021 date.
Future ingestion must apply field-level source integrity/freshness checks rather than treating all official-domain HTML as uniformly authoritative.
